Finally! Google working on fix for Chrome's high RAM usage

I'm not a big fan of Chrome for many reasons.

A: I don't like all the multiple processes. It seems to me like bandaid approach to buggy programming. Palemoon never screws up on me no matter what I throw at it despite having a single process.

B: I am not particularly fond of my browser reporting on anything.

C: I dislike the trapezoid tabs.

D: I hate the fact that Chromium is in damn near everything...Opera=Chromium....Firefox=Chromium....Vivaldi=Chromium....

The only good browser not Chromium based with a decent following and support/compatibility/extensions seems to be Palemoon which is based on Firefox gecko engine and continues to be developed by Moonchild and associates.

The day Opera stopped being Opera and started being Chromium I quit using it. What's the point?

I've been (very reluctantly) using Chrome ever since and the high RAM usage and multiple processes have always bothered me.

I was going to ask what kind of info Chrome sends to Google's "mother ship" but instead I just used Bing to search for my answer, http://lifehacker.com/5763452/what-data-does-chrome-send-to-google-about-me

Felt wrong using google, figured Bing would give me the good "dirt." Turns out, they're not exactly getting much. Pretty much the same info they'd get if you typed a search into google search and considering the address bar doubles as a google search that should be too surprising to anyone.

You should consider changing the default search engine in Chrome, and disabling all the unnecessary options.

DuckDuckGo is improving rapidly. I send my searches there and only use https://encrypted.google.com as a fallback.
Have you tried out Vivaldi? It is the chromium-based continuation by Jon (creator of Opera) himself...

No, I was unaware of that project. Installing it now. Thanks. ;)
